# Beehiiv

We start right after Tyler graduates from college with a failed startup, college debt, no job and living in his parents’ basement… 

## Founding

### Morning Brew {#morning-brew}

**Tyler spent 3.5 years (June 2017 – October 2020\) working at Morning Brew. He started as a contractor but was quickly hired as their second full-time employee.** 

“I graduated with a bunch of student debt and my company didn’t take off. So, I was living in my parents’ basement with literally $2.50 in my bank account. I had put all my eggs in one basket, thinking that this company was going to be a multi-billion dollar success, because you have to be delusional as a founder. I was left with nothing. Fortunately, I was at my parents’ house, so I started building Shopify stores and taking on random freelance gigs as a self-taught developer” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=262)

“I became very fascinated with Shopify. I thought it was such a powerful platform. I ended up doing a lot of freelance work building Shopify sites” [Tyler (Jul 30, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/lZYIRPtU4xQ?t=217)

#### Austin calls Tyler

“My good buddy Austin Rief who is also from Baltimore called me” [Tyler (Jul 30, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/lZYIRPtU4xQ?t=234)

“I was on an hour-long car ride home from DC and Austin was venting \[on the call\] about the business and the opportunity. This was when Morning Brew probably had 30,000-40,000 subscribers. He was debating raising money and going full time or taking a big investment banking job in New York. One thing he said was, ‘Did you know Barstool is making 40% of their revenue through merch?’ or whatever the number was. He was interested in merch, and I said, ‘Dude, I got you.’ Shopify was my thing. I said, ‘Let me help you build,’ because they had some brand affinity with the mug and the logo, and people wanted t-shirts, hats, or coffee mugs. So the first idea was, ‘I'll help you build a Shopify store’” [Tyler (Sep 12, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/Dc4CGW6loPQ?t=126).

“We started talking, and he said [theSkimm](https://www.theskimm.com/) is growing so quickly. They were trailblazers in the newsletter space, with millions of subscribers. They had the [Skimm’bassadors program](https://blog.theskimm.com/all-about-that-bass-ador-828620db7cee), a referral program that worked really well. All these girls in New York who read it loved their ambassador program and were always sharing it. He said, ‘We should imitate that’” [Tyler (Sep 12, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/Dc4CGW6loPQ?t=170)

**Tyler starts with contract work for Austin/Morning Brew (June 2017\)**  
“I straight-faced told him, ‘Yeah, absolutely, no problem.’ Even though I had no idea how to do it. I had $2.50 in my bank account and he offered me $3,000 to do it” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=351)

“For 3 weeks, I was building this referral program, making it up as I went. I had no idea what I was doing and almost quit 5 separate times. At 2 a.m., I’d be up thinking, ‘I lied about being able to do this, and I have no idea how to get past this point.’ I almost texted him to give up but didn’t. I finished it and he paid me $3,000” [Tyler (Sep 12, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/Dc4CGW6loPQ?t=210)

**Tyler kept working for Austin/Morning Brew throughout the summer while applying for other jobs.**  
“Then \[Austin\] said, ‘We have so many other projects to build. If you want to keep working with us throughout the summer while you apply for full-time jobs, let’s do it.’ So I started contracting for them, working 40-60 hours a week, building the website, improving the referral program, and creating different components for the newsletter” [Tyler (Sep 12, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/Dc4CGW6loPQ?t=232)

“That summer, I freelanced for Morning Brew, working 40-60 hours a week building various features. Eventually, Austin asked if I wanted to join them full-time in New York” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=443)

#### Second employee

**Tyler rejects life as a consultant to work full-time as a Morning Brew employee.**    
“I had $120,000 of student debt from paying for school myself. So the safe move was to go to DC, live with my friend, and work at Deloitte as a consultant. I had signed the offer and was set to start in two weeks when Austin reached out and said, ‘What do you think about joining Morning Brew full-time and coming up to New York?’” [Tyler (Sep 12, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/Dc4CGW6loPQ?t=250)

“In retrospect, it seems like a no-brainer. Morning Brew went on to be very successful. But when I joined, they had 50,000 subscribers, two co-founders and a writer in a NYU dorm-room-office thing. I had so much debt and it was such a risk. One of my friends, who I asked for career advice, said, ‘You’re going to be 1 of 50,000 people in that job at Deloitte doing the same thing or the only person in the world building Morning Brew and doing that.’ I completely bet on myself, dropped my girlfriend, left life in DC, and moved to New York within 2 months. That’s how I got into Morning Brew” [Tyler (Sep 12, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/Dc4CGW6loPQ?t=269)

**Austin and Alex gave Tyler massive control and responsibility.**   
“As a small startup, they gave me full control of the inbox and everything that was going on. Every time we pressed send, we would get 500 replies of people being like, ‘I absolutely love this newsletter, I can't start my day without reading it.’ That reader feedback gave me the buy-in that there's something here. You can sell education, you can do advertising, you can do events. There's so much opportunity if you have the attention of these people. And so, one thing led to another, I moved up to New York and joined them back in 2017” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=483)

“I got a few percent equity” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/Dc4CGW6loPQ?t=314)

“I owe Austin and Alex so much. One is they didn’t have the bandwidth to micromanage me and tell me what to do. So, they gave me all of their trust and faith. Like, ‘We trust you, we hired you, just figure out how to grow this newsletter and build this ecosystem.’ And so, I was 22, building the core infrastructure of how we're sending emails, how our writers are using the platform, and how our readers are interacting with our content. I don't have a boss, I don't have a mentor, it's just a figure-it-out situation, which is amazing” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=1173)

**Tyler built Morning Brew’s internal tools: their referral management system, content management system, ad management platform, dashboards and website.**   
“I was building for the internal team. The CMS that we built was for the content team. We built an ad management platform for the ad sales team and the copywriting team used to manage the ad inventory. And we built dashboards for the growth team. At the end of the day I was building tech for 40ish internal employees and some consumer facing stuff” [Tyler (Jul 30, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/lZYIRPtU4xQ?t=3529)

“The CMS we built in-house. Our writers created the newsletter. We made it custom fit to what Morning Brew is. You can drag and drop the stories around. There’s the referral program. Press send in one place, it goes to the website and email. We could’ve pieced together and paid tens-of-thousands of dollars for off-the-shelf software but I took a risk on myself to build it ourselves and it ended up working great” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=898)

#### Bye bye Morning Brew

**Towards the end of Tyler’s 3.5 years at Morning Brew, he pitched Austin and Alex on productizing and white-labeling their tech stack.**  
“I actually pitched to white-label what we built at Morning Brew to Alex and Austin and said, ‘Why don’t we do this? Everyone’s asking us for this software. What if you just gave me 3 months, and we made it so anyone could sign up and use the software we built at Morning Brew? Instead of it being for our employees, it could be for anyone,’ which is Beehiiv essentially” [Tyler (Jul 20, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/lZYIRPtU4xQ?t=4252)

“I didn’t know that they were already in acquisition talks. It’s hard to be in the late eighth-inning of an acquisition and then be like, ‘Oh, we’re actually now a SAAS platform.’ So I understand why they didn’t want to do it. Plus, a lot of media companies have tried to become tech companies and failed. Risk-adjusted, I get it. Morning Brew is working really well as is, so why pivot to being a SAAS company with a 2 person engineering team, led by someone who’s self-taught and has never built a SAAS product before?” [Tyler (Jul 20, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/lZYIRPtU4xQ?t=4271)

**Tyler leaves Morning Brew (October 2020\) to work at [Google](#google). His sudden departure led to a rough patch with Austin and Alex.**  
“There were 3 of us in a closet-sized office for years, just building this business. But in anything with startups and that type of culture, there's a lot of egos and emotion, and there's a lot going on. There was so much to build, and 3.5 years later, I kind of scratched that itch, and we were optimizing the website, which is a little bit less exciting for me. And of course, I have these broad ambitions and an ego of, ‘Hey, I built all this, I want to be paid a lot more, I want more equity,’ and Austin is very pragmatic, and he's like, ‘No, you're four years out of college, this is what the going rate is.’” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=1250)

“Morning Brew was a dream job. I had a ton of responsibilities. Senior leadership team. Figuring things out on the go. Did that for 3.5 years. I joined when we were about 50K-100K subscribers (in 2017\) and grew that to 3.5M when I left. I hired a few engineers and a growth person” [Tyler (Jul 30, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/lZYIRPtU4xQ?t=3472)

“After 3.5 years that ecosystem was very robust. The writing was on the wall that we were legitimizing into a 50+ person company. Not that I didn't want a boss but I knew that there was going to be an incoming head of product from Vice or Vox, and it was going to get more complicated” [Tyler (Jul 20, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/lZYIRPtU4xQ?t=3562)

“I love the 3-30 person company, that was exhilarating to me and there was no red tape and I was calling the shots and doing what I wanted. I learned a lot and got what I needed out of that experience but the writing on the wall was that I wasn't going to be on the senior leadership team forever and that they were going to bring in product managers from other media organizations and me personally, maybe being stubborn, I didn’t want learn from other product managers” [Tyler (Jul 20, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/lZYIRPtU4xQ?t=3582)

“I saw what I could do there and my effectiveness was getting smaller and smaller. The projects were improving the website a little bit which was not as exciting for me. I kinda knew I was ready to try something different” [Tyler (Jul 30, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/lZYIRPtU4xQ?t=3707)

“I left maybe not in the most mature terms. I didn’t just pick up and leave, but I was like, ‘Yo, I got a job at YouTube Music, and I’m out in 2 weeks.’ And I was the first person in the core early team to peace out” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=1308)

“I had no idea that they were in talks with Business Insider to get [acquired](https://www.axios.com/2020/10/29/insider-inc-buys-majority-stake-morning-brew), And, literally, I think the second week on the YouTube Music job, I woke up one morning and got a notification from 20 of my friends: ‘Yo, congrats\! I can't believe Morning Brew just got bought.’ So, I think that also leads to the drama and the emotion tied up. Austin, little did I know, was in hardcore negotiations to make millions and millions of dollars, and now a core person on his team is leaving weeks before” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=1327)

**Austin and Tyler are boys now**  
“Austin and I are boys now. He was our first advisor. He’s also an investor. I was texting him yesterday” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=203)

#### Beehiiv Prototype {#beehiiv-prototype}

**After leaving Morning Brew (October 2020), Tyler worked at ([Google YouTube Music](#google)) until August 2021\. During his 10 months at Google, he was building the Beehiiv prototype on nights and weekends with his two co-founders ([Ben Hargett](https://www.linkedin.com/in/hargettbenjamin/) and [Jake Hurd](https://www.linkedin.com/in/jacob-hurd-%F0%9F%90%9D-1bb869100/)).** 

“I had a week in between Morning Brew and YouTube. I was supposed to go to San Diego and do normal things like relax and travel. I got Covid so I couldn't travel” [Tyler (Jul 20, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/lZYIRPtU4xQ?t=4183)

**Convinces his two co-founders to start building with him.**   
“I’m just sitting in my room in Brooklyn, thinking, ‘What am I going to do for a week? Can’t really go outside, can’t travel.’ I was kind of pissed off that I wasn't in San Diego, so I called [Ben Hargett](https://www.linkedin.com/in/hargettbenjamin/) (co-founder) and said, ‘We’ve always talked about productizing Morning Brew and building out the tech there. What if we just built that?’ We had a few calls, and he brought in [Jake Hurd](https://www.linkedin.com/in/jacob-hurd-%F0%9F%90%9D-1bb869100/), who he went to school with, he became our third co-founder. We mapped it out, and [Ben](https://www.linkedin.com/in/hargettbenjamin/) goes, ‘Dude, it’s a lot of work. That’s pretty damn ambitious to build out a whole email platform that does everything. Morning Brew took us 5 engineers and 3.5 years. Not only do you want to do that, but you also want to make it a platform that anyone can just sign up and start using on their own?’ And that was kind of the start of it, at the end of 2020” [Tyler (Jul 20, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/lZYIRPtU4xQ?t=4412)

**First Google Meet. Discussing specifics. Winter 2020**  
[![][image1]](https://blog.beehiiv.com/p/the-beehiiv-story-chapter-1#:~:text=First%20Google%20Meet%20to%20discuss%20the%20idea%2C%20winter%202020)  
**They started building on nights and weekends. Tyler was full time at [Google (YouTube Music)](#google) and Jake and Ben were still full-time engineers at Morning Brew.**  
“Ten months building at glacial speed because it’s nights and weekends for me and my co-founders” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=2918)

“Beehiiv was a nights and weekends project while they were working at Morning Brew and I was working at [Google](#google). Separate computers, separate everything. I was just working late at night. So we did that for about 10 months. Pretty much the whole time I was at [Google](#google), I was hustling on this on the weekends” [Tyler (Jul 20, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/lZYIRPtU4xQ?t=4459)

“The amount of anxiety of building something very slowly against fully-funded full-time teams (competitors) and I’m kind of battling egos with Alex and Austin who were my good friends and former bosses but I’m also taking two of their four engineers to co-found this company with me and there’s legal implications. I don’t know if I’m waking up with a non-compete or a non-solicit. A lot is going on while also having a full-time job while falling behind in this market while also having this dream vision of ‘I think we can do this and pull it off but each day that we’re not heads down on this we’re getting further and further away from being able to compete.’ It was just a ball of ten months of anxiety” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=2937)

“I did this in the most risky way possible because, at the time, I was still very young in my career and had a ton of debt. I couldn’t just not make money and live in New York or LA while building a company. Plus, our company required software vendors with annual contracts of $80,000. So, we [raised money in August 2021](#seed), and the second the money hit the bank account, I put in my two weeks’ notice at [Google](#google). I started full-time at Beehiiv in early August 2021\. It was me, [Ben](https://www.linkedin.com/in/hargettbenjamin/), and [Jake](https://www.linkedin.com/in/jacob-hurd-%F0%9F%90%9D-1bb869100/) as co-founders (who joined full-time a few weeks after Tyler) and we brought on [Andrew Platkin](#andrew-platkin-\(rip\)) as our initial CTO. So, it was us 4, just grinding and building. Then, we launched in November of 2021” [Tyler (Jul 20, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/lZYIRPtU4xQ?t=4517)

### Thesis

“I can't think about the grand vision after 8:00 p.m. because then I don’t sleep. We have a really talented team, and we have a pretty well-defined roadmap for at least the next 12 to 24 months. I get really excited about what we’re in the process of building” [Tyler (Jul 20, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/lZYIRPtU4xQ?t=5836)

“If there’s a writer who’s going to spend 3 hours writing stories for a newsletter, whether you send it to one person or one-million people, that writer’s work is the same. It’s a fixed cost in terms of time and effort. Our job is to make the other parts easier. The monetization part, so you don’t need a sales team; the growth part, so you don’t need a growth team; the tech part, so you don’t need a tech team. If you’re amazing at writing about whatever you care about, the fact that we should be able to abstract away the tech, growth, and monetization at a very high level so you can focus on reaching your audience. That is the Holy Grail value prop of what we’re doing for newsletters” [Tyler (Jul 20, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/lZYIRPtU4xQ?t=4986)

#### Momentum

“Our kicker was, ‘We’re going to ride the momentum of Morning Brew’s success and you’re going to have a referral program built into it.’ Now it’s a bit more commoditized but that was our initial counter-positioning” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=2906)

#### Validation

“It was pure demand validation. People were asking for the referral program, the CMS, and the total package of what we had built” [Tyler (Jul 20, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=1744)

“We always got a couple hundred replies each day \[at [Morning Brew](#morning-brew)\]. What software are you using?” [Tyler (Jul 20, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=1686)

“The inception of Beehiiv happened way back at [Morning Brew](#morning-brew) because we would always get inbound from readers saying, ‘Your referral program is amazing, the newsletter’s amazing. Can my team or organization use your tech, or how did you build this?’ They were all hoping that we had an off-the-shelf solution to say, ‘Oh, we just use platform X for the referral program,’ or ‘This is the CMS we use.’ But the truth was, we had a custom-built referral program, a custom-built CMS, and a custom-built ad management system. The website was custom-built too. So there wasn’t a simple ‘Hey, just use this.’ It was like, ‘Oh, we built that,’ and you can’t access it” [Tyler (Jul 20, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/lZYIRPtU4xQ?t=4219)

#### Founder-market-fit

“Being the person who led the development and made a lot of the decisions of how it worked and functioned, when people are like, ‘Hey, I want to use this referral program, is there a software you can recommend us off-the-shelf?’ The answer was, ‘No. We built it in-house.” So it didn’t solve their problem. I built that. I know exactly how it works” [Tyler (Jul 20, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=1725)

**3.5 years of seeing newsletter needs up close**  
“We know the pain points. We’ve seen the pain points. I've sat next to teams that were dealing with these pain points, and we’re just building tech to help facilitate those and make it easier. So people can create the content they want to create, build a business around it, monetize, grow, and increase their influence. Meanwhile, we handle the annoying, boring stuff that they don’t feel like doing, and they get all of the upside” [Tyler (Jul 20, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/lZYIRPtU4xQ?t=5588)

**Combined knowledge of working at Morning Brew (small) and Google (big)**  
“The 10,000-foot view of how I’m able to communicate this now is that I went to [Google](#google) for 10 months, got what I needed out of it, and then applied those learnings to Beehiiv. I knew I was rough around process and product management, and I didn’t know what those things really looked like in an organization. I wanted to learn. I learned it as quickly as possible, I was like, ‘Okay, that’s how that works.’ It works really well and scales at a large company with a lot of bureaucracy and process. Now, imagine a 5-6 person startup team. We could hypercharge this and make it so much more efficient. And that’s why we’ve hit the ground running so quickly at Beehiiv” [Tyler (Jul 20, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/lZYIRPtU4xQ?t=4130)

#### White-space

“What we went to market with as counter-positioning was: ‘We have a referral program built into the newsletter.’ Substack didn’t offer it, all the traditional ESPs don’t even think about growth, they just allow you to send emails” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=2880)

**Substack**  
“And then at the same time, Substack just raised $65m (March 2021\) at a [$650m valuation](https://www.axios.com/2021/03/30/substack-andreessen-horowitz-newsletter#:~:text=Substack%20is%20raising%20%2465%20million%20in%20new%20venture%20capital%20funding%20that%20would%20value%20the%20company%20at%20around%20%24650%20million%2C). At the time twitter was just a bunch of angry Substack users” [Tyler (Jul 20, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=1752)

- [Andrew Wilkinson](https://x.com/awilkinson/status/1360021671235604481)  
- [Codie Sanchez](https://x.com/Codie_Sanchez/status/1408473091727052804)  
- [Josh Kramer](https://x.com/jessohackberry/status/1381619399971508228)  
- [Grizwald](https://x.com/grizwald87/status/1390088039968370689)

“Every vendor we looked at was web first. It was, ‘Here’s the SEO features and this is how you publish it to your website. And we were like, ‘No we don’t need to publish it to our website, we need it to look great in Outlook, Gmail and Apple mail.’ The product didn’t really exist in the market” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=883)

**Mailchimp**   
“The analogy I always use is: Mailchimp sold for [$12b](https://techcrunch.com/2021/09/13/intuit-confirms-12b-deal-to-buy-mailchimp/) (September 2021\) and they just send emails. I think what we're building is so much more powerful and ambitious. On top of just sending emails, there are network effects, growth, monetization, there’s sending emails better and a bunch of other data plays” [Tyler (Jul 20, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/lZYIRPtU4xQ?t=5819)

“If Mailchimp can get acquired for [$12b](https://techcrunch.com/2021/09/13/intuit-confirms-12b-deal-to-buy-mailchimp/), our ambition is much broader than the software that they built so I think this can be a massive multi-billion dollar business” [Tyler (Jan 7, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/wQeHYjZNT54?t=1239)

**Net-revenue**   
“We want to be a net revenue income for you. You might pay us $99 a month. But through [boosts](#boosts), [subscriptions](#subscription), and the [ad network](#ad-network), you’re actually making $4,000 or $5,000 from our software. As long as we can keep our users in the black, it’s value-additive in their lives. And that’s what we’re trying to nail as a brand” [Tyler (Jul 20, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/lZYIRPtU4xQ?t=5994)

“There have been decades of email service providers where they’re the cost of doing business. You pay mailchimp $700 per month to send emails. Where I think we have a very interesting opportunity is you might pay us $200-$300 per month but we may be paying you $2,000-$3,000 in earnings from our [ad network](#ad-network) and other features” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=2400)

“We're now creating new monetizable assets and opportunities that didn’t exist before. Email service providers used to be a cost, and now we’re a platform that’s additive to the entire ecosystem” [Tyler (Aug 28, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/SOInHrN_PvA?t=1532)

**Billion dollar outcome**  
“I think we can build a multi-billion dollar business” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=3834)

### DNA

#### Speed

“Today, Beehiiv is known for the velocity at which we relentlessly ship new features. That part of the company DNA stems almost entirely from [Andrew](#andrew-platkin-\(rip\))” [Tyler (May 7, 2024\)](https://mail.bigdeskenergy.com/p/rip-andrew-platkin#:~:text=Brilliant%20doesn%E2%80%99t%20do%20it%20justice.%20I%20have%20never%20come%20across%20someone%20with%20a%20higher%20level%20of%20output%20than%20this%20guy.%20Today%2C%20beehiiv%20is%20known%20for%20the%20velocity%20at%20which%20we%20relentlessly%20ship%20new%20features.%20That%20part%20of%20the%20company%20DNA%20stems%20almost%20entirely%20from%20Andrew.)

“There’s a sense of urgency that percolates through me. Until we own a lot more of this market share, there is so much more to build” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=4913)

“Perfect kills momentum. Like the Reid Hoffman [quote](https://x.com/reidhoffman/status/1050053566574948352), ‘If perfect, you shipped it way too late.’ Unless it's touching money or something that is very fragile, we knowingly ship things 80%-85% done. Not blatantly missing something but not entirely polished. Because the last 10% can take so much time to guess how a user would use this. You can actually short circuit all of that by getting it in their hands and they’ll tell you right away” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=5047)

“There’s an acceptance of good enough and getting it in the users hands where a lot of founders are scared of negative criticism” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=5095)

**Weekly product updates**  
“I send these project updates. I get 40 people telling me what’s wrong with the feature and rather than that hurting my ego, I just synthesize it, put it into a doc and send to to the engineers and they fix it” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=5101)

**Speed as a function of insecurity**  
“When we launched we were the shittiest product in the market because all the competitors had been around for a decade plus and we pieced together something over 10 months” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=1611)

“I still feel that hustle. Our competitors are still 5-15 years ahead of us. There’s so much to do” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=1638)

#### Remote {#remote}

“Thinking through where the best employees live is such a distant and archaic way of thinking about how do we get the best person on our team contributing to what we want to do” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=3714)

“We would not be anywhere near where we are if I only had talent from Los Angeles” [Tyler (Sep 12, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/Dc4CGW6loPQ?list=TLGG6WWzOpMQ_UgxOTExMjAyNA&t=5904)

“We’ve been remote day one, so everything we’ve ever done in our processes is async and remote” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=1453)

“We’re a 100% remote company. So I’m in my room most of the day. For me to be out on a Wednesday outside of the office, it takes a lot for me to not think of the emails I’m missing. We’re fully heads down” [Tyler (Jul 30, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/lZYIRPtU4xQ?t=1220)

#### Meetings

“Meetings are talking about doing things without actually doing them” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=1662)

“It goes to the DNA of what Beehiiv is. My 2 co-founders \[[Ben Hargett](https://www.linkedin.com/in/hargettbenjamin/) and [Jake Hurd](https://www.linkedin.com/in/jacob-hurd-%F0%9F%90%9D-1bb869100/)\] and I are all engineers. We identified a need in a very crowded market. The only thing to do at the time was to put our heads down and build new features” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=1596)

“Four out of our first five employees were all engineers” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=1634)

“I feel most productive personally, and I project it into the rest of the team, when I can put in my headphones and focus on the 10 things I need to do and at the end of the day those 10 things are done” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=1655)

**No meetings on Wednesdays → No meetings on Tuesdays and Thursdays**  
“The early DNA of the company was just being engineers who needed to build. We didn’t need meetings, but eventually, we hired someone in support, community, and growth, and there needed to be some meetings. You quickly realize how context switching totally kills productivity in a small business. So, we did no meetings on Wednesday, and people would always leave Wednesdays saying, ‘I just got so much done.’ One day, someone said, ‘I wish I had Wednesday but twice a week.’ With no hesitation, I said, ‘Say no more, Tuesday and Thursday will be focus days.’ At this point, we were 50 people, so it was kind of hard to change it, but I made sure everyone moved their meetings around so there were absolutely zero meetings on Tuesday and Thursday” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=3510)

“If I could do 5 days a week with no meetings, we’d be so productive. But then you start to play with the fact that we’re entirely remote. We have meetings where we maintain a light, fun culture, where people get to know each other. There are very limited ways to connect with coworkers when you’re entirely remote across 10-12 different countries. If you pull all of that fabric away, what’s left? You’re just on your computer coding. Maybe you’re the most productive person in the world, but you have no idea about anyone else on the team. I’d say it’s a delicate balance” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=3566)

#### Wellness day

**Inspired by Tyler’s time at [Google](#google)**  
“Every single month, we have the third Friday as a wellness day, guaranteeing a three-day weekend every month” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?list=TLGG9RyQsbJm7bQyMDExMjAyNA&t=3482).

#### Outcomes {#outcomes}

“I don’t care if you watch movies all day if you can get your work done. It’s an outputs based business” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=3754)

“One-third of our team is engineers. Engineering is so output-driven. It’s, ‘Here are the 4 features we’re launching next Thursday, and here are the 6 engineers in charge of that.’ It either gets done or it doesn’t. There’s nowhere to hide” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?list=TLGG9RyQsbJm7bQyMDExMjAyNA&t=3741).

**Support team**  
“We can say the same with support, both quantitatively and qualitatively. We have how many tickets are you responding to and your [CSAT score](https://www.zendesk.com.mx/blog/customer-satisfaction-score/)” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=3760)

**Growth team**  
“For growth and marketing, is we need to grow faster, here are our sales objectives and it’s are you delivering or are you not ” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=3769)

“Without micromanaging, shit either gets done or it doesn’t. And if you’re not going to get it done well, we will find someone who can get it done well. That is the shared attitude” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=3780)

“The type of work-culture we’re looking for, it either repels you, as in, ‘I want to do 9-to-5, I don’t want to be held accountable for the outcome of my work.’ Not in a bad way, but some people want to take control over what they’re building and want to make an impact and want to be praised for the work that they do. Some people love that and thrive and there’s enough of them. Some people don’t want the accountability and they’re just not a great fit for the business” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=3887)

“We hired someone out of college who was 20 y/o and he was shipping production code that was touching tens-of-thousands of paying users and making a huge difference within weeks” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=3904)

“We have an [engineer](https://x.com/kiliman) who spent three weeks building a [PWA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Progressive_web_app) feature, turning your newsletter and website into a mobile app. And we launched it and 500 people on twitter are posting about how awesome it is and the CEO and founder of Vercel \[[Guillermo Rauch](https://x.com/rauchg) [said](https://x.com/rauchg/status/1815600074791284785)\] ‘This is an excellent example of PWA being used smartly’” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=3919)

#### Transparency {#transparency}

*Related to [building in public](#building-in-public).*

“But then on the flipside \[of [outcome based](#outcomes)\], everyone at the company has equity in the company. Everyone is a shareholder. I run the business incredibly transparently. Everyone knows how much money we’re making and burning. Everyone knows the bank account” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=3789)

**Weekly team updates**  
“I send a weekly email to the team and there’s probably more complaints in there than there is positivity. But I want everyone to know exactly what is not working in the business because we’ve hired really smart people with trust in them to solve these problems, not to shield them” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=3808)

**Monthly investor updates**  
“I do the investor updates for me. The first investor update ever \[[September 2021](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1VEMBg9xJBBSi4Ragy09shLiI_H34R0dr/view?usp=sharing)\] was kind of, ‘Oh, we just got $2.5m.’ I almost felt like I owed them something as an acknowledgement. I’ve invested in a few small companies and when they take the money I never hear from them in 6 months” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=4574)

**Leverage to raise money fast whenever he needs to.**   
“Because I do send this monthly investor update to about 250 people including investors who passed, I’m constantly projecting our milestones, our revenue, our growth, these big users who are signing on. This leads to a lot of people reaching out, ‘Hey, we’d love to lead your Series A’ or ‘We’d love to invest in your business’” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=4494)

**Also sends investor updates to employees.**   
“I found the exercise of writing the investor update to be very helpful in formulating my thoughts and I also send it to all 75 employees” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=4619)

**The investor updates are also available [for outsiders](https://mail.bigdeskenergy.com/c/beehiiv-investor-journey). Delayed by two years.**    
“The live investor updates that I send to our list of 250, that’s private. But I have open sourced the old ones so you can sign up and receive the first one. As a startup nerd I think this is the coolest thing ever. You put in your email and you get month 1 \[[September 2021](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1VEMBg9xJBBSi4Ragy09shLiI_H34R0dr/view?usp=sharing)\]. And then every single month after that you get October 2021, November 2021, December 2021, January 2022\. So you actually do get an update, it’s just two years delayed. It protects us because we’re not sharing the secrets in real time. But for you it’s almost as if you invested in the seed round kind of following the journey. It’s building in public on my product. It’s the most meta thing ever. I’m not just building in public, I’m doing it on Beehiiv. I copy-pasted the exact thing I sent that month into this automation that you get each month” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=4715)

**Discovered the leverage that comes from public documentation back in Morning Brew.**   
“I learned it from Morning Brew. We would get dozens of people reaching out about how we built the referral program. For the first 15 times I would schedule an hour call and walk them through it because I thought it was cool to share that. And then I was like, ‘Dude I’ve wasted 15 hours talking to random people about how to build this.’ So I spent 10 hours writing a [blog post](https://medium.com/the-mission/how-morning-brews-referral-program-built-an-audience-of-1-5-million-subscribers-3315482c1aa5). Any time someone came to me I sent them to the [blog post](https://medium.com/the-mission/how-morning-brews-referral-program-built-an-audience-of-1-5-million-subscribers-3315482c1aa5)” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=4674)

#### Onboarding

“Every new hire goes through the process of building their newsletter on the platform with all of the bells and whistles. Some actually continue it. Some just do it as the onboarding and that’s it” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=5507)

#### Andrew Platkin (RIP) {#andrew-platkin-(rip)}

“Andrew Platkin was my advisor at [Morning Brew](#morning-brew). When I was 22 y/o at Morning Brew making all of these decisions, Austin was smart enough to recognize that maybe we should get a technical advisor for Tyler to ask questions. So Austin reached out to his investors and introduced us to Andrew who was basically my unofficial technical advisor. He didn’t get paid but he was the person I could reach out to and be like, ‘I have no idea if A or B,’ and he’d be like, ‘This is how you do it.’” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=4018)

“On a Tuesday afternoon I’d be like, ‘Yo I think I just broke everything’ and he would drop what he’s doing at his full time job in Chicago and fix everything I messed up” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=4069)

“10/10 engineer. Unbelievably smart, talented and ambitious” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=4080)

**Tyler invited Andrew to work at Beehiiv during [the pre-launch days](#beehiiv-prototype). He passed away in early May 2022, 6 months after starting the business.**   
“In the [10 months](#beehiiv-prototype) we were building Beehiiv as a side project. I reached out to him with, ‘Hey would you be interested in building this company with us?’ So he ended up being the CTO and we [launched November 2021](https://x.com/denk_tweets/status/1460972355904102404). In May 2022 he ended up passing away. At the time we had six employees. It was a huge gut-check. He knew things that no one else knew how to build. A lot of what we do really well comes from that experience” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=4087)

**Andrew passed away at the beginning of May 2022**  
“Andrew ended up passing away in May of 2022\. At the time, we were six employees. To put a time, place, and feeling into it: it’s so hard to build a startup. We had just raised $2.5m, we had product-market-fit, and we had $20,000 MRR. There was a path forward with momentum. We had something magical and working. Then Andrew passed away at the beginning of May 2022 and that was a huge gut check” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?list=TLGG9RyQsbJm7bQxOTExMjAyNA&t=4148)

“He was owning things that no one else knew how to build. He was a 12/10 engineer. There’s a lot of what we do really well that kind of shines through from that experience. Going through something as absolutely terrible as that makes nothing else in comparison feel like a huge problem. Having 4 engineers quickly teach themselves new coding languages and all the context while we were having scaling issues, while all of our users were complaining about lack of functionality or other problems, was a huge gut check for the business” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?list=TLGG9RyQsbJm7bQxOTExMjAyNA&t=4191)

“After he passed away, we accelerated his vesting period and gave it to his mother. She’s a shareholder which is super motivating” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=4272)

“Going through something as absolutely terrible as that, nothing else in comparison feels like a huge problem” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=4236)

“It’s hard for me to talk about. Whenever I bring up Andrew it’s still very very top of mind” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=4260)

“By far the worst thing that’s ever happened in my life and for the company” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=4298)

### Capital

#### Thoughts 

**Bootstrapping \>\>\>**  
“I respect the hell out of businesses that are bootstrapped” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=4325) 

**Secondary**  
“I won’t share how many shares I own but I haven’t taken any off the table” [Tyler (Jan 7, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/wQeHYjZNT54?t=1065)

**Founder salary**  
“There’s a classic thing of paying yourself very little as a startup founder. I completely disagree with that. I’m able to pour 14-16 hours per day into the startup because I pay myself well enough that I’m not stressed financially to worry about bills and other miscellaneous things that distract you in life. So by giving myself a livable salary I can focus 110% on the business” [Tyler (Jan 7, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/wQeHYjZNT54?t=1092)

**Rasing at a high-valuation changes your exit prospects**  
“Recently, I talked to Austin Rief, the CEO of Morning Brew. And he warned me against raising money because he said, ‘Right now, optionality is key for you. You’ve built a business that's doing $3m ARR in 18 months. There are dozens of companies that would purchase you for $50m and you could walk away with $10-$15 million in the next year.’ That optionality is great as an individual. The second we sign and take venture capital at a $65m valuation, those companies can’t buy us for $50m. We’ve just wiped out a whole tier of companies that might have considered buying us for $50m-$70m. They are no longer in the running to ever purchase us” [Tyler (Aug 28, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/SOInHrN_PvA?t=1353)

**Driven by the investors that said no to investing in the seed round**  
“I’m super competitive. I keep track of everyone who said no to investing in the early days because you’re so early, it’s a kind of, ‘I don’t believe in you.’ Which is what seed investing is. Because you are betting on the team. Which is why I have all our seed investors included on our monthly investor update because it’s personal” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=2167)

#### Seed  {#seed}

**Tyler concluded the [‘10 month pre-launch build period (from the end of 2020 to the summer of 2021)’](#beehiiv-prototype) by raising a seed round. He quit [Google](#google) the moment the money hit his account in August 2021\.**

“If we could’ve built the business bootstrapped we would have. But day one, we’re 26 years old, and we have to pay vendors $50,000-$60,000 per year upfront. So raising the seed round had to happen and we had to hire other people” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=4342)

“We raised a $2.6m round. My goal was to never raise money again. It felt like a lot of money. In summer 2021 we were saying: ‘Here is my hypothesis, here are my co-founders, we all did this at Morning Brew.’ We hinted at what we were going to build and we had a waitlist of 500 people so we had some validation there. ‘Here’s the roadmap we just need some money to pay our vendors, to hire ourselves and to hire an additional 5-6 people’” [Tyler (Aug 28, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/SOInHrN_PvA?t=1272)

**He did it in a month living in a rented house in Venice, LA.**  
“I’m living with my six best friends in this house. I have a full-time job \[[Google \- YouTube Music](#google)\]. Every waking free moment that I have I’m just repeating myself in this living room. It was a month lease that we had. The goal for me was ‘Let's raise money this month.’ And we did it. The money hit the account in August 2021\. I went full-time immediately. My two co-founders \[[Ben Hargett](https://www.linkedin.com/in/hargettbenjamin/) and [Jake Hurd](https://www.linkedin.com/in/jacob-hurd-%F0%9F%90%9D-1bb869100/)\] joined a month later” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=2769)

**There was still tension with Alex and Austin and Tyler.**  
“This was back when walking on eggshells with Alex and Austin. And I was kind of like, ‘Hey we raised money, they \[[Ben Hargett](https://www.linkedin.com/in/hargettbenjamin/) and [Jake Hurd](https://www.linkedin.com/in/jacob-hurd-%F0%9F%90%9D-1bb869100/)\] are my co-founders. We need to start building this thing.’ We gave them an extra 6 weeks to work at Morning Brew to make the transition smoother” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=2802)

#### Series A

**Tyler decided to raise the Series A as a ‘rainy day fund’ for black swan events. He raised $12,500,000 in June 2023\.**

“We had $1,500,000 in the bank. We were spending about $300,000 per month but we were also making around $300,000 per month. So we were kind of break even” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=4359)

**Shooting themselves in the foot.**  
“The first time we shot ourselves in the foot we did something with deliverability or IP, whatever. It basically hurt deliverability pretty noticeably for a subset of our users for 2 weeks. And they were obviously super pissed off. And it wasn’t a band aid fix; we had to let it play out for 2 weeks. It was 2 weeks of people bitching at you every single day and they happened to be our most valuable users” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=4369)

**Realizing Beehiiv’s fragility.**  
“It kind of showed the fragility of the business. My job as a CEO is to ensure we have enough money to keep building. And in the worst case scenario, if this fails, we have enough money to keep pivoting and trying things because we have smart people. It was a real ‘Oh shit moment,’ realizing that we’re more fragile than I thought and at the same time other competitors in the space were reaching out to our top users and offering $10,000 advancements to move to their platform. It was at that moment that I said, ‘Oh shit, we’re under capitalized.’ We can have the better team and the better product but we can just get run over by the competition that’s been around for 10 years or has tens of millions of dollars in their back pocket” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=4416)

“We have such a good thing going with very smart people and an amazing product. I’d hate for a bad month or a black swan event that puts us shit out of luck with 2 months of runway” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=4543)

“What if AI totally wipes out newsletters? Or something happens with Gmail? We have such a talented group of people that with $10,000,000 in the bank we could figure out something else to do. But it always comes down to: ‘Do you have people who are smart, talented, bought in, take pride in their work and are enjoyable to work with?’” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=5816)

**He also used the Series A to hire more people and delegate more tasks.**   
“I’m hoping we’re at a point especially with the Series A fundraising that we can hire and delegate more tasks and I feel like I can step away for an hour without the world being on fire” [Tyler (Jul 30, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/lZYIRPtU4xQ?t=1236)

“I have so much conviction in our team and our vision, in how we build and ship, that I think we can just outperform the competition” [Tyler (Oct 1, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/zVBPBuqMoVc?t=179)	

#### Series B

**The Series B was a deliberate choice to put the pedal to the metal. Tyler raised $33,000,000 in April 2024\.**

“We still had $10,000,000 in the bank. We were burning $300,000-$500,000 per month. It became this classic fork in the road. My gut is: ‘I love bootstrapped, slow and steady.’ But then you start to realize that the paid spend is working. We could ramp this up and get more market share. We’ve actually ignited a lot of competitors in the space to pick up their pace and work harder. It’s actually getting harder” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=5880)

**Fork in the road. Slow and steady OR pedal to the metal**  
“There’s a path forward of, ‘Yes we could inch it out and burn $400,000-$500,000 per month. We’ll close those margins, we’ll work towards break even.’ Or we could really step on the gas and really try to win and dominate in this market” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=5907)

“I think that’s the classic tale of VC in general but ultimately we’re super competitive and we have a ton of conviction in what we’re building and I wanted to accelerate market share, not just slow and steady” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=5920) 

“As part of our Series B fundraise, unconventionally, we reserved $1m of allocation for our most loyal users to invest” [Tyler \- Big Desk Energy (Nov 12, 2024\)](https://mail.bigdeskenergy.com/p/chapter-3#:~:text=As%20part%20of%20our%20Series%20B%20fundraise%2C%20unconventionally%2C%20we%20reserved%20%241M%20of%20allocation%20for%20our%20most%20loyal%20users%20to%20invest.%20Our%20competitive%20advantage%20has%20always%20been%20putting%20our%20users%20above%20all%20else.%20Allowing%20them%20to%20become%20shareholders%20and%20participate%20in%20the%20upside%20was%20a%20no%20brainer%20for%20me.)

### Growth

#### Waitlist 

“I [tweeted](https://x.com/denk_tweets/status/1404817547770449935) right before going out to raise money. That’s when I put my cards on the table and said, ‘I’ve been building a newsletter platform that will not take a cut of revenue, has a referral program, a totally customizable website, and newsletter.’ If that’s something you’re interested in, sign up for our [waitlist](https://x.com/denk_tweets/status/1404817547770449935) here. I just made a Google Form waitlist and got around 500 people to sign up” [Tyler (Sep 12, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/Dc4CGW6loPQ?t=1607)

“We had our waitlist of 500 people, so the easiest, lowest-hanging fruit was hitting up all of them with, ‘Hey, we launched, check it out,’ and me persistently emailing these people and annoying them to move over. I’d say maybe 100 of the 500 moved over at some point in the next 3-6 months” [Tyler (Sep 12, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/Dc4CGW6loPQ?t=2218)

**Tyler constantly talked to 10-15 newsletter operators during the [prototype building days](#beehiiv-prototype).**  
“I had been cultivating a core audience of 10-15 people. I’d ask them things like, ‘Do you think this is a good way to build this?’ I had an internal squad of people I’d bounce ideas off of, show screenshots, and ask, ‘Do you prefer A or B?’ They’d say, ‘Go with B,’ and I’d go with B. It was about cultivating early adopters, and they were pretty big in the newsletter space. I don’t know how big or small the newsletter market is, but I had that kind of network from my Morning Brew days, and that’s what I was working with” [Tyler (Sep 12, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/Dc4CGW6loPQ?t=1645)

#### Angels

“Our [seed](#seed) and angel investors all had newsletters (or most of them did). For example, [litquidity](https://x.com/litcapital), a meme account on [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/litquidity/?hl=en) and [Twitter](https://x.com/litcapital), had his own [exec summary](https://www.execsum.co/subscribe) newsletter that was using a random email provider. We raised money and the first ask is, ‘Look we just started we need a little bit of momentum here’” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=3043)

“We had probably 2 dozen angel investors that had a newsletter of some sort. Some put up a little bit of a fight, they’re like, ‘I have a full business that works on this platform and you just launched a week ago. I’m not sure I’m going to move my entire business that generates revenue.’ That’s why I always give a huge shout out to [litquidity](https://x.com/litcapital). No hesitations, our product is so janky at this point. We just launched. And he picks up 100,000 emails and just drops them in” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=3089)

“As investors, they were financially incentivized to make sure we succeeded, and they were really our early adopters. It sounds so simple, and I don’t know why more startups don’t go to market like this. Why not get investors who are going to be your early customers, because early customers are by far the hardest to get” [Tyler (Sep 12, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/Dc4CGW6loPQ?t=2237)

“You really need early adopters that believe in you, and what’s better than the people who just wrote you a $100,000 check to say, ‘Hey, in order for this to get off the ground, we need some early traction.’” [Tyler (Sep 12, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/Dc4CGW6loPQ?t=2309).

#### Unscalable

“I don’t do this anymore. It’s one of the unscalable things we did in the early days. I used to approve every sender on the platform before they could send. We would ask for their Twitter handle and LinkedIn as an anti-spam measure to check they were legit. I would follow them on Twitter and connect with them on LinkedIn. I did that for an hour and a half every day, which created a multiplier effect” [Tyler (Jul 30, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/lZYIRPtU4xQ?list=TLGG9-Tp0QpUXWwyMDExMjAyNA&t=2697)

#### Logo

“We’re a very consumer facing product. We have ‘built on beehiiv’ on the footer of the email and website. So there’s network effects to getting large users. When we convert someone to move over to our platform and they’re sending to 100,000 readers, that’s 100,000 people that see our logo at the bottom of their footer. That’s a natural network effect that works in our favor” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=3062)

#### Building in public {#building-in-public}

*Related to [Transparency](#transparency)*

**Tyler builds in public to reduce churn and drive top-of-funnel.** 

**Building in public is a way to control the narrative.**  
“A lot of it comes from the insecurities of being a very new product and needing to build whatever narrative you can that people are actually building this product” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=3193)

“People moving over having a good experience, sharing it, knowing that they’re going to get a retweet from me, my co-founders, our house account and it kind of builds this narrative on social media that as an innocent bystander scrolling through your feed you sees 7 people who just moved into Beehiiv and it kind of sets in, ‘Oh everyone is moving to Beehiiv’ It just creates a narrative of a successful product ” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=3233)

**It helps with top-of-funnel awareness.**  
“We ship a lot of new features and that comes from the insecurities of, ‘Yes we launched but we’re missing 20 of the largest features that every competitor has in this market.’ The only way to be able to communicate that we’re working on it is we ship as quickly as we possibly can. We send an email to all of our users that says, ‘Hey we just launched this feature.’ It sends a signal of: ‘Hey you don’t need to churn, we now offer this.’ It reassures existing users. And then we promote it on social, a bunch of people share it and it becomes leadgen. It’s churn reduction and top-of-funnel awareness” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=3283)

“When you ship 2-3 new features every single week then the narrative shifts to, ‘Yes, they’re still missing 10 things but they shipped so many features that by the time I migrate over they’ll probably already have addressed those things. They’re very aware that they’re missing things and they’re addressing them as quickly as possible’” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=3342)

**It reduces churn.**   
“A lot of it is psychology, narrative and building momentum. A lot of it is convincing people not to churn because we are listening to them and building things. And then convincing people that were blocked that we’re aware and prioritizing things that they were previously blocked on” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=3359)

**Tyler’s brand expands outside of newsletters.**  
“If I only tweeted about email newsletters all day, that is a very small segment of the world who actually gives a shit. But if I expand to ‘This is how we hire,’ ‘This is our onboarding philosophy,’ ‘Here’s the milestones,’ ‘Here’s the difficult decisions we’ve made about how we’ve structured our team.’ That now appeals to a very large base of people who are generally interested in entrepreneurship, startups, business and that’s a much bigger market” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=3384)

“If I can win the ear of someone who is just interested in startups and entrepreneurship, because they don’t give a shit about emails but they’re interested about how we run this [remote first](#remote) company, then I have a fan in them, and when they’re at a dinner and someone talks about their email newsletter they can easily be like, ‘Hey, I follow this guy Tyler, he runs this company Beehiiv I think you should give him a shot ” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=3414)

#### Ad network {#ad-network}

“The value we provide is being able to bring you advertisers that are relatable to your audience” [Tyler (Jul 20, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/lZYIRPtU4xQ?t=5525)

**Newsletter side**  
“You have a 20,000 person list because you're amazing at writing about sports, not because you know how to do brand advertising, sales, and monetization. So, how do we allow you to keep writing about sports and allow us to help you monetize?” [Tyler (Jul 20, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/lZYIRPtU4xQ?t=4835)

“As a publisher, I’m writing the newsletter that I was going to write anyway. And I’m getting an opportunity from Netflix to pay me a $2-$3 cost per click. I get the brand validation of having Netflix’s logo at the top of my newsletter. I did no selling, no testing, no copywriting, no reporting and money was deposited into my account just from accepting the ad. So it really is a win-win situation. And once you start using a ton of first party data, we have machine learning engineers building all of these different models, it becomes extremely performant. And basically tapping into untapped inventory that would’ve went unsold previously” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=2343)

**Brand side**  
“And on the brand side: if you want to get in front of women in their 30s because that’s where you are most likely to get conversions, you can come to us and we know based on our best in class 1st party data. Some newsletter operators don’t know what data to collect, how to collect it, or what to ask for. But we can tell brands, ‘We have 8,000 newsletters with the majority of the audience is women in their 30s. We can get you in front of them and diversify your spend.’”  [Tyler (Jul 20, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/lZYIRPtU4xQ?t=4859)

**The Holy Grail: Win-Win-Win**  
“So it’s better for newsletters because they’re getting inbound ad opportunities from brands they probably couldn’t contact on their own or it’s not a core competency. And we can go to brands and say: ‘We can target the people that you want across our network of newsletters based on all of our first party data.’ And it really is at scale a win-win-win that we’re trying to build. That’s the Holy Grail” [Tyler (Jul 20, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/lZYIRPtU4xQ?t=4886)

**Downside for newsletters**  
“What you give up in working with the [ad network](#ad-network) is the narrative of: ‘This is exactly who our audience is.’ You will get a better rate if you’re out in the market negotiating yourself. What you’re getting by working with us is that you don’t have to do that work” [Tyler (Jul 20, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/lZYIRPtU4xQ?t=5474)

“You are writing your newsletter to your 10,000 dental professionals about what is hot in the dental industry, what are different trends, what are different studies and as you’re writing you see an inbound opportunity from [Crest](https://crest.com/en-us/oral-care-products/toothpaste?PasteNeeds=All+Toothpastes) come in and they’re paying you $40 CPM and you can press one button, add it to the newsletter and then we’ll send you a wire for $3,000 a few weeks later and you don’t know anyone at Crest. You didn’t do any of the work, no copywriting, you aren’t reporting, you aren’t doing any tracking. You just press the button” [Tyler (Jul 20, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/lZYIRPtU4xQ?t=5493)

“We only gave you Crest because we know your audience is dental focused. Crest is our customer at this point too. We need to make sure they see a positive ROI. So we’re bringing advertisers to newsletters that make sense” [Tyler (Jul 20, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/lZYIRPtU4xQ?t=5539)

“We don’t do exclusivity. So if you have a relationship at Crest you can do those deals. It’s not like because you’re on our platform you can’t do other deals” [Tyler (Jul 20, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/lZYIRPtU4xQ?t=5561)

“We work backwards from we want all of the newsletter to make money, grow and succeed. We’re building tools to help facilitate that. If you can find ways to make money and grow faster with other tools or your own relationships, we don’t restrict that. We’re just trying to be additive” [Tyler (Jul 20, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/lZYIRPtU4xQ?t=5574)

#### Boosts {#boosts}

“It’s basically a paid recommendation network” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=2454)

“You can recommend other newsletters, and they can recommend you. Every time you sign up for a newsletter, you can see the 5 newsletters that they’re reading or recommending. That’s like a network-effect type play that works really well” [Tyler (Jul 20, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/lZYIRPtU4xQ?t=5703)

“For example, you could say, ‘I’m spending $5 per lead on Facebook or Instagram to grow my email list. I’m willing to pay $3 to anyone on Beehiiv to help drive me subscribers.’ So, you set your CPA at $3 and every newsletter on Beehiiv can see that. They might think, ‘I’m growing by 1,000 subscribers a week. If I push 2% or 5% of that to you and get $3 kicked back to me for every subscriber, then it’s worth it.’ It’s just network effects with people who are willing to pay” [Tyler (Jul 20, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/lZYIRPtU4xQ?t=5718)

“A lot of our roadmap comes back to experiences we had at Morning Brew. There, we put a ton of money into Facebook, Instagram, Google and Snapchat. Our north star was ‘We want to convert new readers to the newsletter that have a high likelihood of opening, reading, and clicking on different content and ads. So we’re looking for quality readers who are engaged.’ So it makes perfect sense that the most quality readers are probably opening their email and reading other email newsletters’” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=2458)

![][image8]

#### Website builder

Tyler [announced](https://x.com/denk_tweets/status/1805616672319193373?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw%7Ctwcamp%5Etweetembed%7Ctwterm%5E1805616672319193373%7Ctwgr%5E61dcc06b15057cfd9f7509297add1cd04c58880e%7Ctwcon%5Es1_c10&ref_url=https%3A%2F%2Fblog.beehiiv.com%2Fp%2Fbeehiiv-acquires-ai-based-website-builder-typedream) the acquisition of [Typedream](https://typedream.com), an AI-based website builder, on [Jun 25, 2024](https://blog.beehiiv.com/p/beehiiv-acquires-ai-based-website-builder-typedream). 

Following the acquisition, Typedream's co-founder and CEO, [Kevin Chandra](https://x.com/kvnchandra), joined Beehiiv to lead their website-building initiatives.

Typedream was the [\#1 product of the month](https://typedream.com/blog/what-we-did-to-get-typedream-1-product-of-the-day-on-producthunt) on Product Hunt and went through [Y Combinator in 2020](https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/typedream).

Kevin Chandra [on what Typedream does](https://archive.is/1QLX2#selection-2097.0-2104.0:~:text=%22Our%20plan%20is,a%20few%20clicks.):

- “Our plan is to be able to do something where if you have a media publication, you don’t need to care about the website at all,”   
- “The AI will take care of it for you.” 

A big part of Typedream’s pitch has been that it leverages AI to help users launch websites without needing to actually write any code. When explaining the rationale behind his acquisition, Denk emphasizes how well-built Typedream’s manual, drag-and-drop web builder is. The goal, he says, is to remove friction from the website-building process, which means incorporating AI but not letting it run the show.

The terms of the deal aren’t being disclosed, but Denk says some of Typedream’s co-founders will be coming over to the Beehiiv team.

“Similar to Substack, we offer a website for our users. They can create content, publish it, and it goes out via email and via web at the same time. We’ve always had a basic website offering, and we’ve realized over the past 12 to 18 months that probably the most common feedback that we would receive is more features, functionality, customization” [Tyler (Jun 26, 2024\)](https://archive.is/1QLX2#selection-2071.0-2071.369:~:text=%22Similar%20to%20Substack,features%2C%20functionality%2C%20customization.%22)
