### Ideas

#### Newsletters

“People always ask: ‘How big does my newsletter have to be before I start monetizing?’ I toss out 10,000 subscribers sounds like a good round number where it at least interested advertisers say: ‘That’s enough people that if we can get 2%-5% conversion that would move the needle a bit for us’” [Tyler (Jul 20, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/lZYIRPtU4xQ?t=5399)

**Newsletter advertisements**  
“It depends on what game you’re playing. If you are trying to build long lasting relationships with these advertisers, you want to deliver as much return to the advertiser as possible. As the newsletter operator you want to be able to sell the vision of why they should advertise” [Tyler (Jul 20, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/lZYIRPtU4xQ?t=5384)

“It’s all about selling the narrative of why that audience is more valuable than advertising on another channel. If you have a newsletter that speaks to 10,000 decision makers at Series A and Series B startups and you know that for a fact from the surveying you’ve done. And you know you have a hold and influence on these people, that’s very valuable. And the alternative of going to Google or Facebook, like how do you target decision makers who run product organizations at a Series A or Series B company on Facebook. The answer is that you probably don’t hit that audience too reliably” [Tyler (Jul 20, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/lZYIRPtU4xQ?t=5417)

**CPM**  
“CPM is amazing for newsletters because it’s straightforward: we have 100,000 people, we charge a $10 CPM, so you're getting $1,000 every time you monetize. That’s what we did at Morning Brew, and that’s what a lot of newsletters do” [Tyler (Jul 20, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/lZYIRPtU4xQ?t=5188)

“$20-$50 is a common range CPM. Depending on how niche your target is. If you’re very niche, you can get up to $100-$200 CPM. It also varies on whether it’s your list size or just the people who are opening. We would always go back and forth at Morning Brew and elsewhere with ‘Do you charge based on people who are opening? Or the list size?’ Because if they don’t open it’s not an impression” [Tyler (Jul 20, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/lZYIRPtU4xQ?t=5340)

**CPA**  
“Brands want CPA because they only pay when someone converts and buys their product. Totally de-risked. Performance based” [Tyler (Jul 20, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/lZYIRPtU4xQ?t=5205)

**CPC**  
“Then, CPC is like the happy middle ground. It’s like: ‘We don’t know what’s going to convert on your website, you might have a terrible landing page, so we’ll just pay you for how many people you drive to our landing page” [Tyler (Jul 20, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/lZYIRPtU4xQ?t=5225)

**Performance advertisers on newsletters**  
“The DTC, performance, direct response, they’re much more analytical in seeing return on ad spend. So for a newsletter, a much bigger pain in the ass to be able to deliver, because they have a shorter span of ‘We need to see results or we’re moving to another channel.’ That’s why a lot of newsletter operators are going niche media. Also why HubSpot bought The Hustle. Because all they need is one conversion and they’re good for a foreseeable future in terms of ROI” [Tyler (Jul 20, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/lZYIRPtU4xQ?t=5238)

**Push vs. pull (framework from Morning Brew days)**  
“The blogger days of going to [cnn.com](http://cnn.com) or [nyt.com](http://nyt.com). There was a time in college when part of my routine, I’d go to [techcrunch.com](https://techcrunch.com/) and read 5-10 stories. It’s what we would call at Morning Brew the push vs. pull. It used to be you have your [ebaumsworld.com](https://www.ebaumsworld.com) or [techcrunch.com](https://techcrunch.com/), whatever. You go to these different websites. There’s a web destination that you go to. And then you realize everyone in the world is so busy. They have their jobs, their responsibilities, they have other things going on but everyone checks email so rather than me having to remember to go to  [techcrunch.com](https://techcrunch.com/) I could sign up for their email newsletter and in the normal routine of my day I check my inbox and there’s the techcrunch newsletter that they’re sending me the top stories. It gets pushed to me. It’s effortless for me as a consumer. Why it’s valuable as a writer or publisher is the exact inverse. You’re meeting people exactly where they are which is in their inbox, checking flight receipts or responding to friends and family and whatever else” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=940)

“Once you get that top-of-funnel, there is the newsletter business which is still primarily ad based but you can also do subscriptions like the Patreon/OnlyFans model. Just charge your readers directly and they have this relationship with you. It also just unlocks that top-of-funnel for whatever else you want to sell them” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=1004)

**Problem with social media algorithms**  
“Facebook sold all these brands and publishers on getting fans or likes on their pages. Because as a business that sold umbrellas, if you get thousands of people that like your page and then you post this new umbrella, maybe it was showing 70% of your fans on their feed. All it took was some product managers realizing they could make more money pushing native posts or community or something else. They changed the algorithm. And now you’re getting 7% of your audience (down from 70%). You don’t really own the algorithm or the distribution” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=1085)

“When I press send to 45,000 people on my list, they all more or less get the email directly from me irregardless of what some feed does. With the caveat that there is spam and that does live in the hands of few black box players which is the shitty part of email but if you do the right thing and follow best practices you’re usually pretty good there” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=1119)

#### Hiring

“We only typically hire full stack engineers” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=4925)

“Maintaining a high bar of the quality of engineer that you’re extending that offer to was also one of the most difficult but biggest cheat codes” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=4998)

### Appendix

#### Google {#google}

**Tyler was a Product Lead at Google (in the YouTube Music team). He joined Google in October 2021, after his 3.5 years at Morning Brew. He quit right at the moment the [Seed](#seed) money hit his account in August 2021\.**

“My roommate at the time was working at Google. He said, ‘Hey, there's a job that opened up at YouTube Music’” [Tyler (Jul 20, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/lZYIRPtU4xQ?t=3721).

**Tyler almost worked at Ramp instead of Google.**  
“It was right at the beginning of Covid and I was actually really interested in fintech so I applied at all these big fintech companies \[[Ramp](https://ramp.com), [Brex](https://www.brex.com/?ref_code=pmk_g_g_19486703726_141821765741_kwd-977611001_643825738047_brex_e_Cj0KCQiA_9u5BhCUARIsABbMSPvZvGBzSRek1jDc1_JYO-qGxaN0TjBUxSsEyDpdFeLzdXAZ7dHQxEkaAiIyEALw_wcB&qgad=643825738047&qgterm=brex&gad_source=1&gclid=Cj0KCQiA_9u5BhCUARIsABbMSPvZvGBzSRek1jDc1_JYO-qGxaN0TjBUxSsEyDpdFeLzdXAZ7dHQxEkaAiIyEALw_wcB), [Pipe](https://pipe.com), etc …\] fintech was hot and I love tech and financial stuff” [Tyler (Jul 20, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/lZYIRPtU4xQ?t=3736)

“In NYC I stumbled into the Ramp co-founder \[[Eric Glyman](https://www.linkedin.com/in/eglyman/), [Karim Atiyeh](https://www.linkedin.com/in/karimatiyeh/), and [Gene Lee](https://www.linkedin.com/in/genejaelee/)\] when they were 25 employees. I saw that what I wanted to do next was be an early employee at a somewhat de-risked startup, so I could get a little bit of equity in a company that I thought would definitely become a unicorn. It wasn’t so risky that it was like the first 5-10 employees, but they were clearly on a growth trajectory. Those were the kinds of companies I was looking for, but I didn’t get any of those jobs” [Tyler (Jul 20, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/lZYIRPtU4xQ?t=3772)

**He worked remote the entire time**  
“I ended up applying to Google and got a job at YouTube Music in early Covid. I never set foot in the Google office, which is part of the perk of working at a company like Google—the cafeteria, the offices, the space—and being able to stumble from one meeting to another and bump into like 5 of the smartest people you'll ever meet” [Tyler (Jul 20, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/lZYIRPtU4xQ?t=3802)

“I was in my tiny apartment, working out of my room, and I knew that I wasn’t going to have the big company culture. But it was an opportunity to join one of the largest, most successful tech companies to ever exist. It also gave me the chance to make a realistic assessment of what I knew. But I didn’t actually know what it meant to be a product manager in a real company. A real company, meaning one where I’m not making my own rules” [Tyler (Jul 20, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/lZYIRPtU4xQ?t=3832).

“I had very bureaucratic very slow moving clear pain points that you can't address cuz you don't have the budget or the buy-in or it's too many friction points but it's Google” [Tyler (Jul 20, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/lZYIRPtU4xQ?t=3919)

“I was on the YouTube Music team, in the underground side of publishing rights and masters—everything related to who gets paid. It was situations like: music is playing in the background of a video for 20 seconds, the publishing rights are owned by a few people, and there is a person watching in Canada. So the rights there are different than in India, Russia, or the U.S. Who gets those 3 cents? But when you multiply it by millions and millions of views, it becomes significant. That was one really interesting aspect—understanding how the music industry works, which is a totally different set of problems and a totally different pace” [Tyler (Jul 20, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/lZYIRPtU4xQ?t=3953)

**Google learnings**  
“What I learned there, which is still applicable, is the process. They had a very well-defined approach: if you were going to launch a feature, you’d do a product requirement document—10-20 pages. It includes the user journeys, wireframes, and what happens when the user clicks on something. P0 means this has to be there for launch, P1 is ‘this would be nice,’ P2 is ‘nice to have,’ and then there are things you launch knowing they’re not perfect, with follow-up tasks for these 10 things. But everything’s well-documented” [Tyler (Jul 20, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/lZYIRPtU4xQ?t=3998)

“I should have done the Google process for my CMS that I built at Morning Brew. You should know every step: what tech you’re going to use, how each piece will fit together, and what the end result will be” [Tyler (Jul 20, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/lZYIRPtU4xQ?t=4027)

“I never had a process at Morning Brew, and I learned it in Google. You’d think something as buttoned-up in process as Google wouldn’t be applicable in a startup, but that’s exactly how we launch every feature at Beehiiv: PRD (Product Requirement Document), technical scoping doc, sign-off by everyone, then build” [Tyler (Jul 20, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/lZYIRPtU4xQ?t=4092)

**Three-day weekend**  
“At the peak of Covid at Google, Sundar introduced a mental health initiative and declared a wellness day – one random free friday to create a 3-day weekend. Everyone thought it was the coolest thing ever, being appreciated for working hard and getting an extra day off. We adopted that at Beehiiv. Every single month, we have the third Friday as a wellness day, guaranteeing a three-day weekend every month” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?list=TLGG9RyQsbJm7bQyMDExMjAyNA&t=3482).

#### Turning down $50m

“If you were to ask me two years ago if we could get acquired in 18 months, would I take $50m? I'd say, ‘You mean I work for 18 months, and there's a $50m exit? 10/10 times, I'm taking that.’ We've been offered to get acquired for that amount and, without hesitation, said: ‘No, we're on to bigger things.’ Once you accept venture capital at a $65m valuation, you're going for a $600m- $1b-plus exit. That optionality, which once was very fruitful and available to me, is no longer there” [Tyler (Aug 28, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/SOInHrN_PvA?t=1408).

“Recently, I talked to Austin Rief, the CEO of Morning Brew. And he warned me against raising money because he said, ‘Right now, optionality is key for you. You've built a business that's doing $3m ARR in 18 months. There are dozens of companies that would purchase you for $50m and you could walk away with $10–$15 million in the next year.’ That optionality is great as an individual. The second we sign and take venture capital at a $65m valuation, those companies can't buy us for $50m. We've just wiped out a whole tier of companies that might have considered buying us for $50m-$70m. They are no longer in the running to ever purchase us” [Tyler (Aug 28, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/SOInHrN_PvA?t=1353)

“I love the grind. That's really why I love doing this. I'm 29, I have so much energy, and I'm so fired up. I actually see the opportunity in what we're building. If we're just starting to accelerate now and have had this success with very little money in the bank, the worst product we've ever had, and have been understaffed from day one, it only gets better. We're now creating new monetizable assets and opportunities that didn’t exist before. Email service providers used to be a cost, and now we're a platform that's additive to the entire ecosystem. I see a multi-billion dollar exit for sure, and that's what I'm chasing” [Tyler (Aug 28, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/SOInHrN_PvA?t=1532).

“The opportunity cost of being stretched for the next 3-5 years of my life is very real. What's the cost of having $15m tomorrow versus chasing $150Mm that's not even guaranteed but will cost you 4 years of stress, anxiety, hustle, and everything else that comes with it? It's a very real trade-off and a very difficult decision, but I think that's true for everyone who turns down a potential acquisition. You're always chasing more, and you can look back in 10 years and feel like an idiot for walking away with nothing, which I've already accepted is a very real possibility” [Tyler (Aug 28, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/SOInHrN_PvA?t=1592).

#### GoDaddy sucks

**This took place on [February 3, 2023](https://x.com/denk_tweets/status/1621614431875776512).**  
“I went to a bachelor party in Cabo and didn't check my emails for 8 hours. Apparently, one of our users was a malicious user and sent a phishing link that got rerouted to our server, which got rerouted to our web hosting, which was GoDaddy. Their security team flagged it and gave me a 24-hour heads-up, which I missed while traveling, and then they just shut down our DNS” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=5194)

“I'm playing beer pong. I'm drunk in Cabo with my friends” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=5160)

“I'm checking in on Slack. I can never fully detach and the engineers are saying, ‘Hey, we got 10 reports of user websites coming down.’ What was actually happening, not even just on our platform which would have been easier to identify, was that a lot of people hosted their websites on the Beehiiv subdomain. Our users’ websites, along with their users and readers, were unreachable. They were slowly shutting down” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=5239)

“We were trying to debug it, but we hadn't pushed any code in 24 hours so we couldn't figure it out. Slowly, everyone's websites started to go down, including our app” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=5269)

“I’m also at a bachelor party, drunk, trying to be with friends. They all go out to dinner and then to the club, and I'm stressed, shirtless, sweating profusely in this house, trying to get in contact with the overseas chat team. Honestly, it was terrible” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=5350)

**Takeaways**  
“Now I know. We use [Cloudflare](https://www.cloudflare.com/). I know all of our vendors, and we have an account manager with all of them. I know if Stripe goes down, it causes these problems. We're aware of them and can make the trade-off of having backups. It was a very tough lesson to learn but a very important one” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=5367)

“Understanding where your weaknesses or vulnerabilities are as a business. You should know any day that you wake up, if Stripe goes down, you're not accepting payments unless you have a fallback, right? But I think every founder should know their blind spots and what happens if something goes wrong. The certainty that you thought was certain suddenly becomes uncertain, and the business would run into a ton of problems” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=5167)

“Obviously, if we had an account manager, this would have never happened. Trying to get in contact with their support and escalating through their overseas chat support in Indonesia to save the business, essentially. I went full nuclear. I'm [tweeting](https://x.com/denk_tweets/status/1621614431875776512) out, emailing, sending a code red to all investors in our investor update, and sharing the whole story of them shutting down our account” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=5279)

“I’m pleading with this person on chat support in Indonesia, saying, ‘If you don't fix this, this entire business is going to go under. We have 10 employees, and they will be unemployed next week if we cannot get our users’ websites and our website back up” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=5305).

“Through pleading and finding the emails and phone numbers of every executive at GoDaddy, I finally got the account back in good standing. We moved off GoDaddy the next day, and now I'm very vocal about absolutely hating GoDaddy” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=5320).

##### BDE newsletter

**Weekly newsletter. Every Tuesday.**  
“Didn't think weekends would perform well for those who use business emails. Friday's have too many holidays and feel like people are often checking out for the weekend ahead. I think Monday's people are catching up on tons of emails and getting back from their weekend. So it left a tossup between T/W/Th and I thought Tuesday was best for people being earlier in the week, motivated, focused, etc” [Tyler (Aug 4, 2024\)](https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:7225887023046234113?commentUrn=urn%3Ali%3Acomment%3A%28activity%3A7225887023046234113%2C7225889725906071552%29&replyUrn=urn%3Ali%3Acomment%3A%28activity%3A7225887023046234113%2C7226010548818059264%29&dashCommentUrn=urn%3Ali%3Afsd_comment%3A%287225889725906071552%2Curn%3Ali%3Aactivity%3A7225887023046234113%29&dashReplyUrn=urn%3Ali%3Afsd_comment%3A%287226010548818059264%2Curn%3Ali%3Aactivity%3A7225887023046234113%29)

#### Tyler’s routines

##### California

For the business I’m in my room, alone, heads-down, 12-14 hours, just grinding and stressed. So my hobbies now are hiking, surfing, yoga, and being outside. I think the southern California lifestyle is pretty elite” [Tyler (Sep 10, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/IfMfAoREp_E?t=849)

##### Daily routine

I do my morning routine, hit the gym, and am back in my room, showered and plugged in by 8:00am” [Tyler (Apr 9, 2024\)](https://mail.bigdeskenergy.com/p/sunshine-rainbows#:~:text=I%20wake%20up%20at%205%3A30am%20every%20day%2C%20Monday%20through%20Friday.%20I%20do%20my%20morning%20routine%2C%20hit%20the%20gym%2C%20and%20am%20back%20in%20my%20room%2C%20showered%20and%20plugged%20in%20by%208%3A00am.)

##### Winters in Medellin

**Tyler spends his winters in [Medellín, Colombia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medell%C3%ADn). Looks like he has a [girlfriend](https://www.instagram.com/p/DA9FnS7SNmX/?img_index=1) there.**   
“When I go to Colombia, it’s focus to the max. I get all of these invites and for the 4 months that I'm in Colombia, it is default no” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=6146)

“I've spent the past 2 winters in Medellín, Colombia. It's funny because I have such little balance in my life. The way I find balance isn't, ‘Oh, maybe I'll stop work at 6 p.m. on a Thursday and go out to dinner.’ It's, ‘Let me pick up and move to an entirely different continent and immerse myself there.’ That is how I've been able to find a bit of balance. I'm also learning Spanish. I've done Airbnbs down in Colombia. I hate the cold, and it sounds funny living in LA, but it gets a little cold in the winter and a totally different cultural experience to be in Colombia, learn a different language, and meet different people” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=6095)

**Thoughts on other businesses (Mailchimp)**  
“For MailChimp’s credit, the free-plan up to 5,000 subscribers, which I think they’ve scaled back since, is brilliant” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=618)

**People he admires (Elon Musk)**  
“There’s a before Twitter Elon and an after Twitter Elon. But what he was able to accomplish and his sense of building these businesses, anyone who's read the books, aside from a pure business acumen, it's hard to refute that what Elon has been able to accomplish is absolutely crazy. Totally redefining industries, making it normal to go to space, making it normal that people drive electric cars, and that's been tried so many times before” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=6016)  
**People he admires (Brian Chesky)**  
“Brian Chesky from Airbnb is a total role model CEO. A standup person. Very thoughtful. I love traveling. Airbnb is a beautifully polished product. I'm a huge fan of the product itself, but the way that he has built the business and conducts himself, I think he's a total class act” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=6044)

“To balance the Elon answer in terms of new Elon, Brian Chesky, I think, is an absolute stud as a CEO and a really product design-driven person” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=6075)

**People he admires (Ben Thompson)**  
“One of my favorite quotes is [Ben Thompson](https://x.com/benthompson?lang=en) saying: ‘The internet is so much bigger than you think it is’” [Tyler (Jul 30, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/lZYIRPtU4xQ?list=TLGG9-Tp0QpUXWwyMDExMjAyNA&t=2691)

“I would actually attribute most of my success in my career to putting myself in situations where I was way over my head because I’m not someone who’s ever going to give up. When you’re not going to give up and you’re way over your head, the only way is up—hustling and figuring it out, whether it means late nights, watching tutorials online, scheduling calls with people who know what they're doing, and learning from them. There are multiple paths to figure out how to solve whatever problem” [Tyler (Sep 12, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/Dc4CGW6loPQ?t=368).

“At the end of the day, I think most content creators care about two things: growing and monetizing. If you can create tools that allow them to grow quicker and monetize more, most content creators, businesses, and publishers are very happy” [Tyler (Sep 12, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/Dc4CGW6loPQ?t=1178)

“My favorite word, I tell everyone this and they make fun of me, is serendipity. Because there are so many chance events that happen in life that open one door and lead to something which leads to another thing” [Tyler (Jul 30, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/lZYIRPtU4xQ?t=727)

“I’m very disciplined with focus. I say no to a lot of things but I’m only in this situation because I happened to say yes to certain things that have opened the door elsewhere” [Tyler (Jul 30, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/lZYIRPtU4xQ?t=746)

“Early in my career, it was almost always yes to everything. If someone reached out on LinkedIn and said, ‘Do you want to chat?’ I’d be like, ‘Yes, let’s do it.’ I had time and the trade off at 21-22 y/o was what doors exist, what relationships could I make. I was a total ‘yes guy’” [Tyler (Jul 30, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/lZYIRPtU4xQ?t=767)

“I’d say in my personal life I’m still very much a ‘yes guy’ but as the business mature saying no is actually power” [Tyler (Jul 30, 2023\)](https://youtu.be/lZYIRPtU4xQ?t=792)

**On firing people**  
“There’s been a few people where there’s a bit of friction in the early days and you just hope magically they’re going to be a different person and start contributing, caring more and working harder but that never happens. And it’s always a moral drainer. When you’re so good at bringing on A players, you actually discredit how annoying it is for them to have to put up with someone who is putting a B+/C- effort” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=5706)

“I’m a people person, it sucks firing people, it sucks admitting that you were wrong and ruining someone’s week, month or career trajectory” [Tyler (Sep 5, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/k2ezi6HM5XQ?t=5782)

**How does Tyler respond to people saying the name beehiiv sucks, all the time?**  
“I am potentially very OCD, and I need a foundation before building. I had the idea with my co-founders that we could build a platform that does this, and then it’s like, 'Okay, what do we do next? Do we start building? What colors do we choose? What’s the foundation?' For me, as a dreamer or someone with inspiration and goals, I need to envision it. Envisioning it means asking, 'What does this look like when it’s successful?' Part of that boils down to the name and what this thing is going to look like one year, three years, or five years from now.” [Tyler (Aug 13, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/h2bvuIPMC0Q?t=2018)

“There was very little thought put into \[the name\]. It really just comes from the idea of a hive of followers—someone with a hive of people following them. We were playing with the word ‘hive,’ and then 'Beehiiv' came up. I thought, ‘That sounds fine. I can clearly see a logo around that’ The name ‘Beehive,’ spelled correctly, was already taken as a URL, as most good URLs are. So, I just played with classic startup spelling, doubled some letters, moved some things around, and we found one that was available for $10” [Tyler (Aug 13, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/h2bvuIPMC0Q?t=2018).

“I also truly believe—and I think we’re a case study of this—that the name doesn’t really matter… If you’re solving a great problem, and your product, platform, or service is considerably better, works well, serves a purpose, and provides value, the name becomes an afterthought” [Tyler (Aug 13, 2024\)](https://youtu.be/h2bvuIPMC0Q?t=2087)
